review: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
Stadacona and Hochelaga are recorded in the 1530s. Champlain's 1603 journey does not establish them as continuing seats. Political affiliations in the northern interior remain unresolved.
https://ontarioarchaeology.org/wp-content/uploads/OA_web_100.pdf
Great Lakes and northern New York
The Deer nation's admission to the Wendat confederacy is usually placed around 1610. The reconstruction distinguishes that later membership. Some western seats are beyond the terrain frame.
https://www.asau.ru/files/pdf/2036197.pdf
Southern New England and Long Island
The Hassanamisco history also identifies Pegan and Nipnet. Their separate seats and jurisdiction around 1600 require further evidence.
https://nipmucnation.org/history
Southern New England and Long Island
Nantucket accounts identify Wanackmamack, Nicornoose, Autopscot and Potconet in connection with 1659. The distribution of authority among their predecessors in 1600 remains open.
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/d4/Nantucket%3B_a_history_%28IA_nantuckethistory01doug%29.pdf
Hudson, Delaware and Susquehanna valleys

Kechemeckes, Little Siconese, Asomoches, Armewamese, Axion, Mosilian, Sewapois, Narraticons, Okanickon and Minguannan also occur in later records. Their circa-1600 seats and relationships have yet to be established here.
https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Gazetteer/Places/America/United_States/_Topics/history/_Texts/WESDDV/5*.html
Hudson, Delaware and Susquehanna valleys
The archaeological labels Shenks Ferry and Monongahela do not establish a single polity for each settlement area. The western and central Pennsylvania interior remains an evidence gap.
https://npshistory.com/publications/choh/aie-v1-2011.pdf
Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont

The Monacan Nation records Tauxnitanias, Shackaconias, Outponcas, Tegoneaes, Whonkentyaes, Stegarakes and Hassinnungas in the 1608 account of Mannahoac tribute. Individual seats await defensible placement.
https://www.monacannation.gov/step-back-in-time.html
Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
The 1607 reconstruction identifies 28–32 groups under Wahunsenacawh. Membership changed through conquest and diplomacy. The map distinguishes the six inherited districts from later evidence.
https://encyclopediavirginia.org/entries/powhatan-d-1618/
Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont

Opiscopank, lower and upper Cuttatawomen, Pissaseck, Nantaughtacund and Onawmanient are individually named in the 1608 voyage region. Local placements and political affiliations at the target date remain under review.
https://www.nps.gov/cajo/getinvolved/upload/SignificanceStatement-2.pdf
Delmarva · researched, extent unresolved
Tockwogh and Ozinies/Wicomiss: the NPS distinguishes plausible town sites, a river association, and contested land. Which areas between the Chester and Sassafras were governed by each polity in 1600?
https://www.nps.gov/cajo/learn/upload/CAJO_FINAL-ICL-REPORT_2023_0314-508.pdf
Southern Delmarva · researched, authority unresolved
Accomack and Accohannock have separately documented cores. The strength of their political relationship at the target date and the northern reach toward Pocomoke remain open.
https://www.dhr.virginia.gov/pdf_files/AC-081_Historic_AH_Survey_Eastern_Shore_2017_CRAI_report.pdf
St. Lawrence · researched, seasonal use unresolved
Iroquet met allies near the Richelieu but wintered upriver. The meeting place cannot supply the location or extent of a homeland.
https://www.biographi.ca/en/bio/iroquet_1F.html
Western Long Island and lower Hudson · researched, extent unresolved
Canarsee, Tappan and Wiechquaeskeck appear in later records. Which contact-period land-use areas correspond to political jurisdiction before colonial land transactions?
https://www.nan.usace.army.mil/Portals/37/Appendix%20A8_Tier%201%20Cultural%20Resources_SEP2022.pdf
Middle Eastern Shore · researched, earlier affiliation unresolved

A 1669 act locates Choptank land on the south bank. It postdates the target by nearly seventy years. Distinct Choptank government and its relationship to Kuskarawock in 1600 cannot be reconstructed from that tract.
https://msa.maryland.gov/megafile/msa/speccolm/m3000/m3100/m3173/pdf/m3173-1777.pdf
Georgian Bay · researched, internal division unresolved

Bear and Cord were founding Wendat nations. The Penetanguishene assessment places its study site in Bear territory, but assigning the intervening shores to Bear, Cord or Rock around 1600 requires contemporary settlement sequences.
https://penetanguishene.ca/media/zwqkxsa1/2-stage-1-and-2-archaeological-assessment-august-9-2022-138-rse.pdf
Northern and western margins · unresolved divisions
Nbisiing and Nitaskinan now have homeland cores. The family territories within Nitaskinan, the Erie constituent polities and the inland divide between Wenro and Erie remain unresolved.
https://chautauquacountyny.gov/sites/default/files/inline-files/erie_studies_vol10_no2_012.pdf
Central Pennsylvania · dated land use

Archaeology places earlier Susquehannock settlements on the North Branch and later concentration in Lancaster County. Assigning the entire intervening interior to the southern polity in 1600 would merge distinct settlement periods.
https://www.millersville.edu/sa/land-acknowledgment/native-summary.php

records.name: Haudenosaunee Grand Council
records.region: Great Lakes and northern New York
records.evidence: Onondaga country was the meeting region of the confederate council. The marker locates the region; the council site moved over time.

records.name: Seneca
records.region: Great Lakes and northern New York
records.evidence: Original schematic of the Genesee valley and western Finger Lakes, following the west-to-east arrangement in the Smithsonian's circa-1600 teaching map. The perimeter generalizes the core area.

records.name: Cayuga
records.region: Great Lakes and northern New York
records.evidence: Original schematic of the Cayuga Lake country, following the west-to-east arrangement in the Smithsonian's circa-1600 teaching map. The perimeter generalizes the core area.

records.name: Onondaga
records.region: Great Lakes and northern New York
records.evidence: Original schematic of the central New York around Onondaga, following the west-to-east arrangement in the Smithsonian's circa-1600 teaching map. The perimeter generalizes the core area.

records.name: Oneida
records.region: Great Lakes and northern New York
records.evidence: Original schematic of the Oneida Lake and the uplands to its south, following the west-to-east arrangement in the Smithsonian's circa-1600 teaching map. The perimeter generalizes the core area.

records.name: Mohawk
records.region: Great Lakes and northern New York
records.evidence: Original schematic of the Mohawk River valley, following the west-to-east arrangement in the Smithsonian's circa-1600 teaching map. The perimeter generalizes the core area.

records.name: Wendat · Bear nation
records.region: Great Lakes and northern New York
records.evidence: The archaeological assessment places Attignawantan villages across the Penetang peninsula in western Wendake and dates settlement there before 1600. This core follows the peninsula between Nottawasaga and Severn sounds. The internal division with Cord communities to the southeast remains uncertain.

records.name: Wendat · Cord nation
records.region: Great Lakes and northern New York
records.evidence: Founding member in Wendake. Location indicates the regional homeland.

records.name: Wendat · Rock nation
records.region: Great Lakes and northern New York
records.evidence: Joined the confederacy around 1590. Champlain recorded the chief Atironta at Cahiagué in 1615; location approximate.

records.name: Attawandaron (Neutral confederacy)
records.region: Great Lakes and northern New York
records.evidence: The assessment describes a late-sixteenth-century shift of western communities east of the Grand River. The outline represents the contact-era core from the lower Grand and western Lake Ontario into the Niagara peninsula. The constituent village territories and eastern frontier with Wenro are unresolved.

records.name: Wenro
records.region: Great Lakes and northern New York
records.evidence: The Erie Studies reconstruction describes successive Erie and Wenro occupation before the 1638 displacement. The temporal order is clearer than the location of their shared frontier specifically in 1600.

records.name: Erie communities
records.region: Great Lakes and northern New York
records.evidence: Southern Lake Erie shore. The regional designation does not resolve the individual constituent towns.

records.name: Kichesipirini · Tessouat
records.region: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
records.evidence: Morrison Island on the Ottawa River was a political and trading center. Tessouat appears in accounts from 1603–13.

records.name: Iroquet's people
records.region: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
records.evidence: Diplomatic meeting area at the Richelieu–St. Lawrence junction around 1609–10. This marker indicates a rendezvous, not a capital.

records.name: Batiscan's community
records.region: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
records.evidence: Algonquin political leadership in the Trois-Rivières region, documented by 1611. The marker locates the region.

records.name: Anadabijou's Innu community
records.region: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
records.evidence: Meeting at Pointe Saint-Mathieu near Tadoussac in 1603. This documents leadership at the gathering, without defining a frontier.

records.name: Bessabes' Penobscot alliance
records.region: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
records.evidence: Penobscot Nation recounts the 1604 meeting with Bashabez on the Penobscot, as far inland as Kenduskeag. The outline marks the lower river core associated with that near-contemporary account. Its ends approximate the river reach; the wider alliance had no documented enclosing frontier here.

records.name: Peskotomuhkati (Passamaquoddy)
records.region: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
records.evidence: Peskotomuhkati history explicitly identifies the Skutik watershed and Passamaquoddy Bay as traditional territory. This outline follows the eastern lakes, lower Skutik and bay approach. Near-contact accounts name Ouagimou; they do not establish that this individual governed the whole Nation.

records.name: Secoudon's Wolastoqiyik community
records.region: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
records.evidence: Secoudon appears as a Malecite chief in the early French accounts. The point is a regional locator for the lower Wolastoq.

records.name: Chouacoët · Onemechin
records.region: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
records.evidence: Onemechin and Marchin met visitors at Saco in 1606. The marker indicates the documented meeting community.

records.name: Missisquoi
records.region: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
records.evidence: Western Abenaki community at the northeastern end of Lake Champlain. The outline follows the lower Missisquoi and adjacent shore.

records.name: Winooski
records.region: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
records.evidence: The Vermont archaeological account distinguishes the Winooski and Missisquoi bands. This point marks the lower Winooski.

records.name: Cowasuck
records.region: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
records.evidence: Upper Connecticut Valley around Cowass and the Great Oxbow. The outline follows the valley near the principal village.

records.name: Pigwacket
records.region: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
records.evidence: Upper Saco intervales around Fryeburg. An approximate valley core is shown.

records.name: Pennacook
records.region: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
records.evidence: Middle Merrimack around present-day Concord. The extent of later alliances cannot establish a circa-1600 frontier.

records.name: Sokoki
records.region: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
records.evidence: Middle Connecticut River, near the southern Vermont–Massachusetts reach. Regional locator; the historical name has had varying uses.

records.name: Pokanoket
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: Sowams and the eastern shore of Narragansett Bay. Wampanoag sachem Ousamequin is directly documented in 1621; the outline shows the local core.

records.name: Patuxet
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: Plymouth harbor community occupied before the early seventeenth-century epidemics. Its separate political status in 1600 is unresolved.

records.name: Mashpee
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: Upper Cape Wampanoag community. The administrative boundaries of later Mashpee do not establish the older extent.

records.name: Nauset
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: Outer Cape communities associated with Nauset. The drawn core follows the outer arm and excludes the western Cape.

records.name: Mystic / Pawtucket
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: Northern Massachusetts Bay leadership associated with Nanepashemet, killed in 1619. The Mystic valley is a regional locator.

records.name: Neponset
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: Southern Massachusetts Bay community on the Neponset River, subsequently documented under Chickataubut.

records.name: Narragansett
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: Core mainland west of Narragansett Bay. The Pawcatuck frontier is described as contested; the outline stops short of assigning it exclusively.

records.name: Cowesett
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: Community along the western shore of upper Narragansett Bay. Later accounts describe tribute relations with Narragansett.

records.name: Shawomet
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: Warwick area. Later accounts identify Shawomet separately in Narragansett tributary relations.

records.name: Pocumtuck
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: Deerfield and middle Connecticut River intervales. The polygon marks the confluence area.

records.name: Hassanamisco
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: Nipmuc community in the Grafton area. The marker locates the homeland; precise local jurisdiction in 1600 remains unresolved.

records.name: Wangunk
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: Middle Connecticut bend. Later testimony describes a network of towns under related sachems.

records.name: Tunxis
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: Farmington River community, named in accounts of Wangunk diplomatic and kinship relations.

records.name: Quinnipiac
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: The historical reconstruction places the homeland along the Sound between West Haven and Madison, reaching inland toward Woodbridge, Cheshire and Durham. The polygon follows this coastal and estuarine country; its inland edge approximates the reported extent before dispossession.

records.name: Pequot
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: The Nation identifies a pre-European homeland between the Niantic and Pawcatuck rivers. This coastal core includes the lower Thames and Mystic estuaries. The inland edge is schematic. Later expansion and conflict around Misquamicut do not establish an exclusive frontier east of the Pawcatuck in 1600.

records.name: Western Niantic
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: Niantic Bay regional placement. Later political relations with Pequot do not establish an exact earlier frontier.

records.name: Shinnecock
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: South Fork community around Shinnecock Bay, one of several local political communities documented on eastern Long Island.

records.name: Montaukett
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: Eastern South Fork. This outline indicates the Montauk peninsula core.

records.name: Corchaug
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: Southold identifies the Corchaug with the North Fork and Cutchogue as a principal place. The core covers the necks around Cutchogue between Long Island Sound and Peconic Bay. Later land records and the fort localize this longstanding occupation; its exact reach in 1600 is unresolved.

records.name: Mohican
records.region: Hudson, Delaware and Susquehanna valleys
records.evidence: Upper Hudson core south of Albany and along the river. Later records give better evidence for internal leadership than survives for 1600.

records.name: Wappinger
records.region: Hudson, Delaware and Susquehanna valleys
records.evidence: East bank of the middle Hudson. Core around the Wappinger Creek drainage; affiliation of neighboring local groups varied.

records.name: Esopus
records.region: Hudson, Delaware and Susquehanna valleys
records.evidence: The refuge history reconstructs the pre-European Waronawanka homeland across the Rondout and Wallkill valleys. It identifies Moodna Creek toward Cornwall and a southwestern limit near the Shawangunk ridge crossing opposite Minisink country. The outline follows these named reaches; the northern closure is approximate.

records.name: Hackensack
records.region: Hudson, Delaware and Susquehanna valleys
records.evidence: Local community in the lower Hackensack River area. Seventeenth-century names are used retrospectively; authority over adjoining communities in 1600 is uncertain.

records.name: Tappan
records.region: Hudson, Delaware and Susquehanna valleys
records.evidence: Local community in the west bank near the Tappan Zee area. Seventeenth-century names are used retrospectively; authority over adjoining communities in 1600 is uncertain.

records.name: Wiechquaeskeck
records.region: Hudson, Delaware and Susquehanna valleys
records.evidence: Local community in the lower Hudson east bank area. Seventeenth-century names are used retrospectively; authority over adjoining communities in 1600 is uncertain.

records.name: Canarsee
records.region: Hudson, Delaware and Susquehanna valleys
records.evidence: Local community in the western Long Island around Jamaica Bay area. Seventeenth-century names are used retrospectively; authority over adjoining communities in 1600 is uncertain.

records.name: Sanhickan
records.region: Hudson, Delaware and Susquehanna valleys
records.evidence: Regional placement at the Delaware falls at Trenton. Later Dutch-era records distinguish local bands along the Delaware; the perimeter and succession circa 1600 are uncertain.

records.name: Mantese
records.region: Hudson, Delaware and Susquehanna valleys
records.evidence: Regional placement at the lower Mantua Creek area. Later Dutch-era records distinguish local bands along the Delaware; the perimeter and succession circa 1600 are uncertain.

records.name: Passayunk
records.region: Hudson, Delaware and Susquehanna valleys
records.evidence: Regional placement at the lower Schuylkill. Later Dutch-era records distinguish local bands along the Delaware; the perimeter and succession circa 1600 are uncertain.

records.name: Brandywine community
records.region: Hudson, Delaware and Susquehanna valleys
records.evidence: Regional placement at the Brandywine and Christina confluence. Later Dutch-era records distinguish local bands along the Delaware; the perimeter and succession circa 1600 are uncertain.

records.name: Great Siconese
records.region: Hudson, Delaware and Susquehanna valleys
records.evidence: Regional placement at the Swanendael, near Lewes. Later Dutch-era records distinguish local bands along the Delaware; the perimeter and succession circa 1600 are uncertain.

records.name: Ramcock
records.region: Hudson, Delaware and Susquehanna valleys
records.evidence: Regional placement at the Rancocas Creek area. Later Dutch-era records distinguish local bands along the Delaware; the perimeter and succession circa 1600 are uncertain.

records.name: Susquehannock
records.region: Hudson, Delaware and Susquehanna valleys
records.evidence: Lower Susquehanna valley settlement corridor upstream of Chesapeake Bay. Smith encountered a delegation in 1608. The polygon represents the valley core.

records.name: Piscataway
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: Moyaone and the Maryland shore of the Potomac. The tayac's influence linked several settlements. Polygon indicates the immediate river core.

records.name: Nacotchtank
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: Anacostia River town identified in the 1608 reconstruction. Its relationship to the Piscataway tayac around 1600 is uncertain.

records.name: Patuxent
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: Chiefdom on the Patuxent. The polygon follows the middle and lower river core.

records.name: Tockwogh
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: Smith visited a fortified town in 1608. The NPS study identifies alternative south-bank Sassafras sites, questions control near the mouth, and distinguishes contested ground. The point marks the river reach; neither a town-site candidate nor the study boundary establishes the limits of Tockwogh territory.

records.name: Ozinies / Wicomiss
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: The NPS study considers Ozinies and Wicomiss likely related names. Smith did not meet them. The Chester River association supports this regional locator; the boundary with Tockwogh and the exact political relationship are unresolved.

records.name: Nanticoke
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: Kuskarawock in the 1608 voyage identifies a near-contemporary Nanticoke river community. The cultural landscape study connects ancestral settlements and traditional use along the river into Delaware. This core follows the tidal valley; the wider study area includes neighboring waterways and is not a political perimeter.

records.name: Accohannock
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: The cultural survey identifies Occohannock Creek as a settlement district and describes a relationship with the Accomacks. Smith distinguishes the two places in the early contact period. The shape follows the tidal creek and nearby shores. Their degree of political independence in 1600 remains unclear; later Nassawadox settlement is excluded.

records.name: Accomack
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: Virginia DHR identifies the south shore of Old Plantation Creek and adjacent lands as Accomack country. The outline follows the lower creek and bayside of the southern peninsula. Smith’s early-contact geography supports this core near 1600; the cross-peninsula extent and northern frontier are uncertain.

records.name: Patawomeck
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: Virginia bank of the Potomac around Potomac Creek. Its diplomatic relationships shifted during the early seventeenth century.

records.name: Mannahoac
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: Upper Rappahannock political network described in 1608. Amorolek named several affiliated towns. The outline indicates the river corridor above the falls.

records.name: Monacan
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: James River Piedmont communities above the fall line. The regional outline is a reconstruction of the central river corridor.

records.name: Tsenacomoco
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: Wahunsenacawh's paramount chiefdom. Werowocomoco is the locator. The six inherited districts form its early core; the larger 1607 alliance developed through expansion.

records.name: Powhatan town
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: One of the six inherited districts. Marker locates the James River falls district; the precise frontier is unknown.

records.name: Arrohateck
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: One of the six inherited districts. Marker locates the James below the falls district; the precise frontier is unknown.

records.name: Appamattuck
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: One of the six inherited districts. Marker locates the lower Appomattox district; the precise frontier is unknown.

records.name: Pamunkey
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: One of the six inherited districts. Marker locates the lower Pamunkey district; the precise frontier is unknown.

records.name: Youghtanund
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: One of the six inherited districts. Marker locates the upper Pamunkey district; the precise frontier is unknown.

records.name: Mattaponi
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: One of the six inherited districts. Marker locates the Mattaponi River district; the precise frontier is unknown.

records.name: Chickahominy
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: River communities governed by a council of elders. Shown separately from Wahunsenacawh's inherited chiefdoms.

records.name: Paspahegh
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: At Jamestown’s founding in 1607 the Paspahegh occupied multiple towns along the James on both sides of the Chickahominy mouth. This core follows the north shore of the James across that confluence to Jamestown Island. It does not project later colonial grants backward.

records.name: Weanock
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: Tidewater chiefdom documented by 1607. The point locates the district; its exact extent and date of incorporation around 1600 remain uncertain.

records.name: Kiskiack
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: Tidewater chiefdom documented by 1607. The point locates the district; its exact extent and date of incorporation around 1600 remain uncertain.

records.name: Nansemond
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: The Nation identifies the twenty-mile Nansemond River as its homeland and describes membership in Tsenacomoco. This core follows the tidal valley inland from Hampton Roads toward Suffolk, covering the village country occupied at English arrival. The inland margins are approximate.

records.name: Warraskoyack
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: Tidewater chiefdom documented by 1607. The point locates the district; its exact extent and date of incorporation around 1600 remain uncertain.

records.name: Quiyoughcohannock
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: Tidewater chiefdom documented by 1607. The point locates the district; its exact extent and date of incorporation around 1600 remain uncertain.

records.name: Kecoughtan
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: Tidewater chiefdom documented by 1607. The point locates the district; its exact extent and date of incorporation around 1600 remain uncertain.

records.name: Weskarini
records.region: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
records.evidence: Petite Nation, Rouge and Lièvre tributaries north of the Ottawa. Outline indicates the lower tributary region, where the group is placed in early seventeenth-century accounts.

records.name: Atikamekw Nehirowisiwok
records.region: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
records.evidence: Nitaskinan is the ancestral territory across the boreal Saint-Maurice country. This outline represents its upper river and lake core around Manawan, Wemotaci and Opitciwan. It does not allocate the family hunting grounds or imply that the modern communities governed these districts in 1600.

records.name: Nanrantsouak / Norridgewock
records.region: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
records.evidence: Upper Kennebec community near present-day Old Point.

records.name: Arosaguntacook
records.region: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
records.evidence: Androscoggin River people. Point locates the river corridor rather than an identified chiefly residence.

records.name: Agawam · Connecticut Valley
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: The regional survey places the core between Enfield Falls and South Hadley. Outline follows those floodplains.

records.name: Nonotuck
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: Connecticut River intervales near Northampton and Hadley; the marker locates the valley community.

records.name: Squakheag
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: Northfield reach of the Connecticut, a distinct northern settlement core.

records.name: Woronoco
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: Community on the Westfield River, west of the Agawam floodplains.

records.name: Aquinnah
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: One of four major sachemships recorded on Noepe in the seventeenth century. The point locates the district; earlier boundaries remain uncertain.

records.name: Taakemmy
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: One of four major sachemships recorded on Noepe in the seventeenth century. The point locates the district; earlier boundaries remain uncertain.

records.name: Nunnepog
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: One of four major sachemships recorded on Noepe in the seventeenth century. The point locates the district; earlier boundaries remain uncertain.

records.name: Chappaquiddick
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: One of four major sachemships recorded on Noepe in the seventeenth century. The point locates the district; earlier boundaries remain uncertain.

records.name: Nottoway
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: Regional placement on the Nottoway River around the coastal plain–Piedmont transition. The source locates the people without delineating chiefly jurisdiction.

records.name: Meherrin
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: Meherrin River regional placement. Boundaries among its early local communities remain uncertain.

records.name: Matouweskarini
records.region: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
records.evidence: The assessment identifies the Madawaska from its headwaters to upstream of Stewartville as this historical Algonquin band’s homeland. The polygon follows the occupied river corridor past the lakes and Calabogie. Adjacent Ottawa tributaries are excluded.

records.name: Kinounchepirini
records.region: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
records.evidence: Bonnechere River group in the Ottawa watershed. The record supports a river affiliation.

records.name: Nipissirini
records.region: Great Lakes and northern New York
records.evidence: Nipissing First Nation places Nbisiing at the center of its territory at seventeenth-century contact. The shape connects the lake, French River and northern lake country toward Temagami and Obabika. Connecting edges are approximate.

records.name: Quinsigamond
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: The Hassanamisco Nipmuc Nation identifies this band on its contact-period map. Marker locates the Lake Quinsigamond area.

records.name: Nashaway
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: The Hassanamisco Nipmuc Nation identifies this band on its contact-period map. Marker locates the Nashua confluence near Lancaster area.

records.name: Assabet
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: The Hassanamisco Nipmuc Nation identifies this band on its contact-period map. Marker locates the Assabet River area.

records.name: Quaboag
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: The Hassanamisco Nipmuc Nation identifies this band on its contact-period map. Marker locates the Quaboag Pond and river area.

records.name: Paugussett
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: Lower Naugatuck–Housatonic confluence. Land records document the community later in the seventeenth century.

records.name: Chesepian
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: Great Neck and Lynnhaven region at the southern mouth of Chesapeake Bay. Archaeological and early historical evidence places a community here before Jamestown.

records.name: Chowanoke
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: Chowan River district under Menatonan in the 1580s. This southern margin entry uses the earlier English expedition as its dated anchor.

records.name: Sakonnet
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: Local Wampanoag community on the eastern shore of the Sakonnet River, around Little Compton.

records.name: Eastern Niantic
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: Southwestern Rhode Island coastal district. Later alliances and named sachems are better documented than the political frontier in 1600.

records.name: Unkechaug
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: The historic resource study identifies continuous Unkechaug occupation and extensive holdings in southern Brookhaven. The polygon shows the mainland shore around the lower Forge River and Mastic. Continuity supports a core near 1600; later estate and reservation lines cannot establish its earlier limits.

records.name: Cape Ann / Beauport
records.region: Southern New England and Long Island
records.evidence: Champlain recorded the community at Gloucester harbor in 1606. Its political perimeter remains uncertain.

records.name: Rappahannock
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: The Tribe identifies Topahanocke in 1607, north-bank towns visited in 1608 and south-bank hunting grounds. Both banks of this middle tidal reach are included. The dates support a contact-era core; neither the hunting limit nor a surveyed boundary survives.

records.name: Moraughtachund
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: Community identified during the 1608 voyages. The point indicates the lower Rappahannock region. Its precise earlier district is uncertain.

records.name: Wicocomoco
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: Community identified during the 1608 voyages. The point indicates the Virginia shore near the Potomac mouth region. Its precise earlier district is uncertain.

records.name: Chicacoan / Sekakawon
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: Community identified during the 1608 voyages. The point indicates the Northern Neck along the Potomac region. Its precise earlier district is uncertain.

records.name: Pocomoke
records.region: Chesapeake, Delmarva and Virginia Piedmont
records.evidence: The Nation describes a paramountcy spanning Somerset and parts of adjacent Maryland, Virginia and Delaware. The shape shows a core around Pocomoke Sound and the lower river, inside the wider homeland described in its history. The source combines homeland and influence; the tributary roster and outer reach specifically in 1600 remain uncertain.

records.name: Wolastoqiyik
records.region: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
records.evidence: The Nation describes a homeland predating colonial borders, centered on the Wolastoq watershed and adjoining lands and waters. The outline traces the upper forks, Madawaska and Tobique approaches and the lower river to the Bay of Fundy. It generalizes the divides; Secoudon was one early-contact leader within this homeland.

records.name: Tionontati
records.region: Great Lakes and northern New York
records.evidence: Archaeological occupation by about 1580 and the 1616 multi-village account bracket the target date. This core follows the escarpment settlements southwest of Nottawasaga Bay. The assessment describes shared occupation with Odawa; the outline is nonexclusive. Internal Deer and Wolf districts remain undivided.

records.name: Minisink
records.region: Hudson, Delaware and Susquehanna valleys
records.evidence: The NPS study identifies a precolonial homeland on both sides of the upper Delaware centered around Minisink Island. This strip follows the inhabited valley between the Port Jervis vicinity and its possible southern limit at the Water Gap. Upland Munsee-speaking neighbors are separate.

records.name: Gespe’gewa’gi
records.region: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
records.evidence: The Mi’gmawei account describes the district north of the Miramichi system including the Acadian and Gaspé peninsulas. The mainland outline follows that northern New Brunswick–Gaspé reach. It depicts the traditional district as a retrospective reconstruction; the precise inland divide in 1600 is unresolved.

records.name: Canibas (Kennebec)
records.region: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
records.evidence: The county account retrospectively describes Kennebec country on both banks from the Androscoggin confluence to Moosehead Lake. It distinguishes Norridgewock, Taconnet and Cushnoc within it. The outline follows this river-and-lake corridor; the 1866 source does not establish fixed internal districts or one ruler in 1600.

records.name: Taconnet
records.region: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
records.evidence: The Kennebec County account distinguishes this local group at Waterville. Its retrospective placement does not delimit a separate jurisdiction circa 1600.

records.name: Cushnoc
records.region: Ottawa, St. Lawrence and Wabanaki country
records.evidence: The Kennebec County account distinguishes this local group at Augusta. Its retrospective placement does not delimit a separate jurisdiction circa 1600.
